note: These are the ones that bite the first stranger who signs up.

items.title: Email sign-in is capped at 2 messages an hour
items.detail: Supabase's built-in mailer is development only, and the app now offers email as a way in. The third person to request a link in an hour gets nothing. Needs Resend or Postmark wired in: a config change, no code.

items.title: Errors are shown but never recorded
items.detail: A crash raises the fatal banner and names the function, so the user sees it. Nothing is sent anywhere, so we never learn it happened. Needs a table plus a hook on the existing error listeners; no new vendor.

items.title: Legal pages predate half the app
items.detail: privacy.html and support.html were written before clips, live sessions, push notifications and photos existed, and use a different design language from the app. Apple requires the privacy policy to match what is actually collected.

items.title: Onboarding has never been walked as a genuinely new account
items.detail: Name, goal, detail, pace, plan, then pairing. Every path exists but has only ever been used by accounts that already had data. Empty states for a truly fresh account need the same pass the rest of the app got.

note: A direction has been reviewed and picked. Nothing here is live, and none of it blocks anyone until it is built for real.

items.title: The tiles-plus-sheet goal picker is a prototype, not the real onboarding step
items.detail: Mo compared the bubble cluster against two other directions after opening every bubble at once and finding 52 items cannot share one screen at any spacing, then picked tiles-plus-sheet: nine categories always visible as a grid, tap one for its full checklist in a bottom sheet, multi-select persists across categories. It runs for real in the sandbox walkthrough (renderGoalTilesPrototype / initGoalTiles in index.html), on the real nine-category research content, not placeholder, but Continue only toasts (verified in the current source: protoGoalCtaBtn.onclick is toast-only) and nothing is written anywhere. profiles.goal_bubble and goal_child now EXIST in production (confirmed via information_schema, migration applied), and the engine already reads them ahead of the legacy goal string when present, so storage is no longer what is blocking this. What is still missing on top of wiring Continue: the picker only captures which bubble/child, not an amount or a deadline, and resolveGoal() needs amountLb/byDate to produce anything for the honest-pace-line entry elsewhere in this list. The gallery's static Choosing a goal page still shows the earlier bubble concept and has not been rebuilt to match this direction.
items.where: index.html, renderGoalTilesPrototype / initGoalTiles; scripts/make-states.mjs Choosing a goal page is stale, still shows bubbles

items.title: Limits and injuries is built; the joint table is coaching judgement, unread by a physio
items.detail: Built for real on 2026-09-10, both ends. Nothing on this screen is placeholder any more: renderLimitsPage / initLimitsPage import BODY_AREAS and EQUIPMENT_OPTIONS from mo-knowledge/engine/limits.mjs at runtime rather than hard-coding them, so a limit is only ever offered if the plan can honour it (Pull-up bar, Squat rack and Bench are gone; No machines, which the engine CAN honour, is finally there). "Does anything hurt" is the same purchased Rive figure Focus areas uses, front and back, with its own controllers and generation counter; a tapped muscle resolves to the nearest joint or joints through an explicit fourteen-group table (LIMIT_GROUP_JOINTS: chest/shoulders/lats -> shoulder, traps -> neck + shoulder, biceps/triceps -> elbow, forearms -> elbow + wrist, abs/obliques/lowerback -> lowerback, glutes -> hip, quads/hamstrings -> hip + knee, calves -> ankle) and paints those groups in var(--partner), the app's existing caution tint. The eight chips mirror the figure and either half can be tapped. "No equipment at all" is exclusive both ways. The free-text line is capped at 120 characters and is stored, shown back and never parsed, on purpose. Save writes profiles.limits = { hurts, missing, note, updated_at } through the same upsert path saveFocusGroups uses, and generateWorkout already sends it, so a marked shoulder really does come back as a plan with no overhead pressing and no dips (verified headless against the sandbox engine: meta.limits.hurts carried shoulder and meta.limits.excludedCount was non-zero). Reachable from a Setup row under Focus areas, and offered exactly once elsewhere: a quiet line under a freshly generated plan, which stops appearing the moment the question is answered, skipped or dismissed, since limits === null is what "never asked" means. WHAT IS LEFT: the muscle-to-joint table above is coaching judgement written from scratch, exactly like joint-load.mjs's own 159 rows, and neither has been read by a physio; until one has, none of it should be described to a user as medical advice, and the screen deliberately never phrases anything as a medical question. Onboarding still never asks, which is the intended design, so an account that never generates a plan and never opens Setup stays at null forever.
items.where: index.html, renderLimitsPage / initLimitsPage / saveLimits / paintLimitsSubtitle, LIMIT_GROUP_JOINTS (unreviewed coaching judgement), revealGeneratedPlan's gen-nudge; mo-knowledge/engine/limits.mjs and joint-load.mjs; profiles.limits (live column)

items.title: The body focus picker is in Setup, never in onboarding
items.detail: Built for real on 2026-09-09: Setup now has a Focus areas row that opens the picker as a settings page, and Save writes profiles.focus_groups and focus_chosen_at, which mo-knowledge/engine/focus.mjs reads to give each picked group 1.4x its weekly sets — confirmed live: a real generate call's meta.focus came back populated, not null. Body impact's muscle viewer got the same save path behind a Focus on this button. Uses the actual purchased figure (knowledge/anatomy/rive-body.mjs, human_anatomy_advanced_v3.0.riv), the same asset Body Impact and the workout builder already render. A tap marks or unmarks the whole 14-group it belongs to (RIVE_TO_APP_GROUP / APP_GROUP_TO_RIVE_MUSCLES, painted in the app accent green on both artboards, front delts and rear delts both from either one). Went through a tap-to-zoom pass and then a pinch-to-zoom pass; neither turned out to be wanted, so there is no zoom at all, tapping never moves the camera. Four is the cap, so Full body is gone and only Clear all is left. What is still not built: onboarding never asks. Somebody who never opens Setup never picks a focus, so the engine sees null for every new account, and the goal's own priority is all it has to go on.

items.title: The engine already suggests a swap for every exercise; nothing offers it
items.detail: Verified live against the real engine, not a spec: a generated plan's first exercise (Lat Pulldown) came back carrying swap: "Negative Pull-Up" and alternatives, a ranked list of up to three with a one-line why each ("Same movement, same supporting muscles, no equipment needed"). exercise_swaps exists in production (confirmed via information_schema) with the shape the engine session described (email, entry_date, planned_exercise, chosen_exercise, source), and currently holds zero rows, confirming nothing writes to it yet. No button, sheet or menu anywhere in index.html reads ex.swap or ex.alternatives on either the reveal sheet or the in-session exercise card. This is the measured half of preference learning the limits entry above deliberately deferred to here; the data to build it now exists on both ends, only the middle (a UI to offer the three alternatives, and a write on pick) is missing.
items.where: index.html, revealGeneratedPlan (reveal sheet) and renderSession (in-session exercise card) — neither reads ex.swap/ex.alternatives; exercise_swaps table (live, empty)

items.title: The honest pace line renders, but nothing currently feeds it a number
items.detail: revealGeneratedPlan already shows honest text above the exercise list when non-null (the gen-step paragraph, index.html) — that half is built and live. But generateWorkout()'s payload never sends goal_bubble, goal_child, or any amount/date, and the engine's resolveGoal() (mo-knowledge/engine/goal-engine.mjs) can only build a timeline from exactly those (amountLb, byDate) or from the legacy goal string with no numbers at all. Verified against the live sandbox on Mo's own fixture account, which has an ACTIVE dated goal (user_goals: lose weight, target 182 lb by day+60) — the real generate call still came back meta.goalSource: "legacy" and honest: null. The number the honest line needs already exists in user_goals (target_value/target_date) for anyone who set one the old way, and will exist properly once the goal tiles picker below is wired and starts asking amount/deadline per bubble; either source would work, but the payload currently forwards neither.
items.where: index.html, generateWorkout (the fetch body never includes user_goals fields, goal_bubble, or goal_child); mo-knowledge/engine/goal-engine.mjs, resolveGoal

note: Nothing here can move without an account, a click, or a decision only you can make.

items.title: Sign in with Apple needs the Developer account
items.detail: Apple requires it once any social login is offered, so it blocks App Store submission. The keys cannot be generated without the paid account. The sign-in screen already has room for the button.

items.title: Jawa is still not a collaborator on the repo
items.detail: Her CODEOWNERS entries point at @jawaabdulal now, but a CODEOWNERS line does nothing until she has repo access. The deploy token cannot add her: it is fine-grained with no Administration permission.

items.title: meridian-web-studio has push access and I do not know who that is
items.detail: A second collaborator with write access to the repo, account created 2026-08-01, no activity on it. Worth confirming who it is or removing it before real users exist.

items.title: Photo retention was never decided
items.detail: Raised in the strategy meeting and left open. Proof photos expire after 30 days. Progress photos tied to a goal have no policy at all, and storage cost was explicitly called a real constraint.

note: Real features that a PWA genuinely cannot do. They all arrive with the same Capacitor step.

items.title: The timer stops when the app is backgrounded
items.detail: Deliberate today, so time asleep is not counted, but the ask was for it to keep running like a navigation app. Needs genuine background execution, which the web cannot give.

items.title: Hands-free voice logging
items.detail: Costed 2026-09-06. Safari has never shipped the speech recognition API, so this cannot be built as a PWA at all. Native gives Apple's on-device Speech framework, but foreground only: push to talk, never always listening. Camera hand gestures are the one option that works in the web app today.
items.where: Capacitor, or MediaPipe in the web app

note: Known, chosen on purpose, and written down so the reasoning is not lost.

items.title: Every write still refetches every table
items.detail: loadAll() runs after almost every write. It is one parallel batch now, and it no longer repaints Home when Home is not on screen, but it still refetches everything rather than updating what changed. Fine at current volume.

items.title: Two tables are fetched in full, unbounded
items.detail: fit_entries and exercise_logs are read whole. Deliberately not windowed: personal records need a true all-time max per exercise and the calendar needs the true first entry ever, so a rolling window would make both silently wrong. Indexed on (email, entry_date) in the meantime.

items.title: The cron secret is inlined in the database
items.detail: Vault is unavailable on this project, so the shared secret sits in the cron job commands and inside the live-start trigger function body. Anyone with database access can read it. Accepted for now; it is not a user credential.

items.title: The gallery does not cover the workout builder or Setup
items.detail: Updated 2026-09-10: Body ("Reading your body") and Progress ("Looking back", with the Consistency/Strength/Volume cards) were added to the static gallery and are no longer missing. Still not in here: the workout builder screens (choose/generate/manual-build/plan-week — the choose screen alone pulls roughly 78 lifted dependencies, far heavier than Body's 29, which is why it was deferred rather than attempted) and all of Setup. Both are covered instead by the sandbox (/sandbox.html), which is now the primary review surface (see the next entry) and runs the real functions against fixture data rather than a static capture.
items.where: scripts/make-states.mjs; sandbox.html covers the gap interactively

items.title: The static gallery is being wound down in favor of the sandbox
items.detail: states.html (scripts/make-states.mjs) was how UI got reviewed through early September: every screen lifted from index.html into still frames, so it could not describe the app wrong, only fail to include something. The sandbox (/sandbox.html, sandbox-data.js, sandbox-steps.js) replaced it on 2026-09-07 and is stronger in the way that matters most: it runs the real app on a writable fake Supabase client, so a screen is reached by tapping through the app rather than posed for a capture, and a journey step can drive real functions (startWorkout, toggleSet, generateWorkout against the real engine) rather than only render one. New screens should get a sandbox journey step, not a new gallery state. The gallery is not deleted yet — some content (the milestone badge design sheet, and the old "Choosing a goal" bubble-picker prototype the entry above references) still only exists there — but new work should default to the sandbox first.
items.where: sandbox.html, sandbox-data.js, sandbox-steps.js vs. states.html, scripts/make-states.mjs

items.title: Two new sheets are unverified visually
items.detail: The encouragement composer and the askForName sheet that replaced the browser prompts passed the boot check and reuse the app's existing composer pattern, but have not been screenshotted. The browser harness kept getting killed the day they shipped.

items.title: Two of the 11 milestone badges lean on a proxy, not a real record
items.detail: Bodyweight Bench compares a bench press log against the most recent scale weigh-in, not the body weight at the moment of that specific set, since the app has never recorded one alongside the other. 1 Year reads the accepted partnership's responded_at, which is real, but nothing else about a pairing's history is tracked, so if that ever needs correcting there is no second source to check it against. Both are honest best-efforts, verified against realistic fixture data (run node scripts/badge-check-test.mjs), not guesses. Fifteen more badge ideas (rest-day-safe consistency ones, a comeback PR, cheering counts, evenly-matched weeks) are still only written down, with no icon and no check function.

note: Kept so they do not come back around as fresh ideas.

items.title: No music integration
items.detail: Showing what your partner is listening to via Spotify was overruled in the strategy meeting: music apps already play in the background, people use different services, and it is not core. Do not build it.

items.title: Live streaming is not the cheering feature
items.detail: Deliberately not FaceTime or a live stream, which was agreed to be too expensive. A short clip that loops on their session screen and then disappears was the chosen shape, and it shipped.
